```{r}
# Function to subset the columns for the preparation of Mutation ID 
prepare_structure_mut_id_columns <- function(df, chain_name = "1") {
  filtered <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(aa_mut_class) & aa_mut_class != "Synonymous",
      !is.na(aa_mut_wt) & aa_mut_wt != "*",
      !is.na(aa_mut_sub) & aa_mut_sub != "*",
      !is.na(aa_mut_pos)
    )

  message("Filtered rows: ", nrow(filtered))
  
  result <- filtered %>%
    mutate(
      
      aa_mut_id    = paste0(aa_mut_wt, aa_mut_pos, aa_mut_sub),
      ddmut_mut_id = paste(chain_name, aa_mut_id)
    )

  message("Final rows: ", nrow(result))
  return(result)
}
```

### 2) Load and process Predictions
RSA data process
```{r}
# Function to calculate Spearman correlation per gene x RSASA baselines
compute_rsasa_performance <- function(
  df,
  predictors,
  gene_col = "aa_mut_gene",
  response_col
) {

  #library(dplyr)
  #library(purrr)
  #library(tibble)

  # ---- helper: map predictor to clean name ----
  get_predictor_name <- function(pred) {
    case_when(
      pred %in% c("RSASA_complex", "dRSASA_complex") ~ "RSA (complex)",
      pred %in% c("RSASA_monomer", "RSASA_monomer_rescaled") ~ "RSA (monomer)",
      TRUE ~ pred
    )
  }

  df %>%
    group_split(.data[[gene_col]]) %>%
    map_dfr(function(df_gene) {

      gene_name <- unique(df_gene[[gene_col]])

      map_dfr(predictors, function(pred) {

        predictor_name <- get_predictor_name(pred)
        predictor_input_modality <- "RSA Baselines"

        # ---- missing predictor ----
        if (!pred %in% names(df_gene)) {
          return(tibble(
            gene_name = gene_name,
            predictor_name = predictor_name,
            predictor_input_modality = predictor_input_modality,
            model_type = "Spearman",
            metric = c("Spearman_r", "Spearman_p", "Spearman_R2"),
            value = NA_real_
          ))
        }

        x <- df_gene[[pred]]
        y <- df_gene[[response_col]]

        keep <- !(is.na(x) | is.na(y))
        x <- x[keep]
        y <- y[keep]

        # ---- insufficient data ----
        if (length(x) < 2 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
          return(tibble(
            gene_name = gene_name,
            predictor_name = predictor_name,
            predictor_input_modality = predictor_input_modality,
            model_type = "Spearman",
            metric = c("Spearman_r", "Spearman_p", "Spearman_R2"),
            value = NA_real_
          ))
        }

        # ---- compute correlation ----
        sp <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x, y, method = "spearman"))

        tibble(
          gene_name = gene_name,
          predictor_name = predictor_name,
          predictor_input_modality = predictor_input_modality,
          model_type = "Spearman",
          metric = c("Spearman_r", "Spearman_p", "Spearman_R2"),
          value = c(
            unname(sp$estimate),
            sp$p.value,
            unname(sp$estimate)^2
          )
        )
      })
    })
}


# Function to run Spearman Correlation cleanly
# 1) the minimal version to calcualte spearman correlation
compute_spearman_by_gene <- function(
  df,
  predictor_col,
  fitness_col,
  group_cols = "aa_mut_gene",
  min_score = NULL
) {

  library(dplyr)

  # ---- Check predictor exists ----
  if (!predictor_col %in% names(df)) {
    stop(paste("Predictor column not found:", predictor_col))
  }

  # ---- Filter NA ----
  df <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[predictor_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[fitness_col]])
    )

  # ---- Optional threshold ----
  if (!is.null(min_score)) {
    df <- df %>%
      filter(.data[[predictor_col]] > min_score)
  }

  # ---- Compute correlations ----
  df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_cols))) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),

      r = {
        x <- .data[[predictor_col]]
        y <- .data[[fitness_col]]

        if (length(x) < 3 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
          NA_real_
        } else {
          suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, method = "spearman"))
        }
      },

      R2 = r^2,

      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# 2) a robust version to handle control when group_cols = NULL
compute_spearman_by_gene <- function(
  df,
  predictor_col,
  fitness_col,
  group_cols = "aa_mut_gene",
  min_score = NULL
) {

  library(dplyr)

  # ---- Check predictor exists ----
  if (!predictor_col %in% names(df)) {
    stop(paste("Predictor column not found:", predictor_col))
  }

  # ---- Filter NA ----
  df <- df %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(.data[[predictor_col]]),
      !is.na(.data[[fitness_col]])
    )

  # ---- Optional threshold ----
  if (!is.null(min_score)) {
    df <- df %>%
      filter(.data[[predictor_col]] > min_score)
  }

  # ---- Handle empty data ----
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(n = NA, r = NA, R2 = NA))
  }

  # =====================================================
  # CASE 1: NO grouping (technical control)
  # =====================================================
  if (is.null(group_cols)) {

    x <- df[[predictor_col]]
    y <- df[[fitness_col]]

    r <- if (length(x) < 3 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, method = "spearman"))
    }

    return(
      tibble::tibble(
        n = nrow(df),
        r = r,
        R2 = r^2
      )
    )
  }

  # =====================================================
  # CASE 2: GROUPED (ΦX / ProteinGym)
  # =====================================================
  df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group_cols))) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),

      r = {
        x <- .data[[predictor_col]]
        y <- .data[[fitness_col]]

        if (length(x) < 3 || var(x) == 0 || var(y) == 0) {
          NA_real_
        } else {
          suppressWarnings(cor(x, y, method = "spearman"))
        }
      },

      R2 = r^2,

      .groups = "drop"
    )
}


# Function to transform to long format
transform_corr_results <- function(
  df,
  gene_col = "aa_mut_gene",
  gene_name_col = "gene_name"
) {

  # ---- detect available metrics ----
  metric_cols <- intersect(c("r", "R2", "p"), colnames(df))

  df %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of("n")) %>% 
    dplyr::rename(!!gene_name_col := dplyr::all_of(gene_col)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::all_of(metric_cols),
      names_to = "metric",
      values_to = "value"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      metric = dplyr::recode(
        metric,
        r  = "Spearman_r",
        R2 = "Spearman_R2",
        p  = "Spearman_p"
      ),
      model_type = "Spearman"
    )
}
```

Process prediction results
- correct aa positions for proteins F and J
```{r}
# Function to shift aa positions in mut id
shift_mutant_position <- function(
  df,
  mutant_col,
  new_col = "aa_mut_id",
  shift = 1
) {

  df[[new_col]] <- stringr::str_replace(
    df[[mutant_col]],
    "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])",
    ~ paste0(
        stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")[,2],
        as.integer(stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")[,3]) + shift,
        stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")[,4]
      )
  )

  df
}

# Function to shift specific positions
shift_specific_mutant_position <- function(
  df,
  mutant_col,
  new_col = "aa_mut_id",
  shift = 1,
  pos_min = -Inf,
  pos_max = Inf
) {

  df[[new_col]] <- stringr::str_replace(
    df[[mutant_col]],
    "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])",
    ~ {
      m <- stringr::str_match(.x, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")
      wt  <- m[,2]
      pos <- as.integer(m[,3])
      sub <- m[,4]

      pos_new <- ifelse(
        pos >= pos_min & pos <= pos_max,
        pos + shift,
        pos
      )

      paste0(wt, pos_new, sub)
    }
  )

  df
}
```

## MSA data 
### 1) MSA statistics
- load MSA result tables
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(fs)

# define the root directory
msa_root <- "/Users/hwei/Desktop/phix_WGM/data/predictors_data/Input_MSA"
#msa_root <- "data/MSA/EVcoupling_MSA"


# find all statistics files
msa_stat_files <- dir_ls(
  path = msa_root,
  recurse = TRUE,
  regexp = "_alignment_statistics\\.csv$"
)

length(msa_stat_files)


# read and parse
msa_alignment_statistics <-
  purrr::map_dfr(
    msa_stat_files,
    function(file){

      # read statistics file
      df <- read.csv(
        file,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )

      path_parts <-
        strsplit(
          normalizePath(file),
          .Platform$file.sep
        )[[1]]

      # database
      database <-
        path_parts[
          grepl(
            "^EVcouplings_MSA_a2m",
            path_parts
          )
        ][1]
      
      database <-
        sub(
          "^EVcouplings_MSA_a2m_",
          "",
          database
        )
      # protein
      protein_folder <-
        path_parts[
          grepl(
            "_EVcouplings_MSA_a2m$",
            path_parts
          )
        ][1]
      
      protein <-
        sub(
          "_EVcouplings_MSA_a2m$",
          "",
          protein_folder
        )
      
      # bitscore
      align_idx <-
        which(path_parts == "align")
      
      bitscore_folder <-
        path_parts[align_idx - 1]
      
      bitscore <-
        sub(
          "^TARGET_b",
          "",
          bitscore_folder
        )

      # hash folder
      hash_folder_index <-
        which(path_parts == protein_folder) + 1

      hash_folder <-
        path_parts[
          hash_folder_index
        ]

      df %>%
        mutate(
          database = database,
          protein = protein,
          bitscore = bitscore,
          hash_folder = hash_folder,
          statistics_file = file
        )
    }
  )


# check loaded data 
msa_alignment_statistics %>%
  select(
    database,
    protein,
    bitscore,
    num_seqs,
    N_eff
  ) %>%
  head()




```



### 2) Statistics (Meff, Meff_L, Quality)
Load and plot the Meff (Meff/L) by proteins as the bitscores increase
```{r}
# load raw data
phix_MSA_EVcouplings_raw <- read_csv("./data/predictors_data/Input_MSA/phix_MSA_EVcouplings_results.csv")
#phix_MSA_EVcouplings_raw <- read_csv("data/MSA/phix_MSA_EVcouplings_results.csv")

# process raw data
head(as.data.frame(phix_MSA_EVcouplings_raw), 5)


# remove unused rows
phix_MSA_EVcouplings <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings_raw %>%
  slice(-(1:2)) %>%
  mutate(dataset = str_extract(Jobs, "(?<=EVcouplings_).*")) 

 
# split results to Meff and Meff/L 
seq_cols <- grep("^Sequences", names(phix_MSA_EVcouplings), value = TRUE)
qual_cols <- grep("^Quality", names(phix_MSA_EVcouplings), value = TRUE)

bitscores <- seq(0.1, 0.9, by = 0.1)

for(i in seq_along(bitscores)) {
  
  seq_col  <- seq_cols[i]
  qual_col <- qual_cols[i]
  b        <- bitscores[i]
  
  phix_MSA_EVcouplings <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings %>%
    
    mutate(
      !!paste0("Meff_b", b) := as.numeric(
        str_extract(.data[[seq_col]], "^\\d+")
      ),
      
      !!paste0("Meff_L_b", b) := as.numeric(
        str_extract(.data[[seq_col]], "(?<=\\()[0-9.]+")
      ),
      
      !!paste0("quality_b", b) := as.numeric(.data[[qual_col]])
    )
}


# drop original result columns
phix_MSA_EVcouplings_clean <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings %>%
  select(
    Protein,
    Jobs,
    dataset,
    Download,
    starts_with("Meff_b"),
    starts_with("Meff_L_b"),
    starts_with("quality_b")
  ) %>%
  rename(
    protein = Protein,
    database = dataset
  )

# transform to long format
phix_MSA_EVcouplings_long <- phix_MSA_EVcouplings_clean %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(Meff|Meff_L|quality)_b"),
    names_to = c(".value", "bitscore"),
    names_pattern = "(Meff|Meff_L|quality)_b(.*)"
  ) %>%
```

## Load VEP Prediction
Data of the predictors results in .csv or .txt files;

### 1) ESCOTT
- Tekpinar M, David L, Henry T, Carbone A. PRESCOTT: a population aware, epistatic, and structural model accurately predicts missense effects. Genome Biol. 2025 May 6;26(1):113. doi: 10.1186/s13059-025-03581-y. PMID: 40329382; PMCID: PMC12054230.
```{r}
# Function to load ESCOTT data
load_escott_benchmarking_data <- function(file_path) {

  # ---- read file ----
  df <- read.delim(
    file_path,
    header = FALSE,
    sep = "",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # ---- shift WT annotation row right ----
  df[1, ] <- c(NA, as.character(df[1, -ncol(df)]))

  # ---- split WT row and score rows ----
  wt_row   <- df[1, ]
  score_df <- df[-1, ]

  # substitutions (a, c, d, ...)
  subs <- score_df[[1]]
  score_df <- score_df[, -1]

  # force numeric scores
  score_df[] <- lapply(score_df, as.numeric)

  # ---- extract WT info (aligned to score columns) ----
  wt_vec <- as.character(wt_row[-1])
  wt_vec <- wt_vec[!is.na(wt_vec)]

  wt_aa  <- sub("[0-9]+", "", wt_vec)
  wt_pos <- seq_along(wt_aa)

  # ---- long-format transform ----
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)

  out <- score_df %>%
    mutate(sub = subs) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -sub,
      names_to = "col",
      values_to = "score"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      col_idx = match(col, colnames(score_df)),
      pos     = wt_pos[col_idx],
      mutant  = paste0(wt_aa[col_idx], pos, toupper(sub)),
      aa_mut_id = mutant,
      ESCOTT = score
    ) %>%
    select(mutant, aa_mut_id, pos, score, ESCOTT)

  return(out)
}
```

### 3) RSALOR, Structure + MSA
- The rsalor package combines structural data (Relative Solvent Accessibility, RSA) and evolutionary data (Log Odd Ratio, LOR from MSA) to evaluate effects of missense mutations in proteins. It computes the RSA*LOR score for each single-site missense mutation in a target protein by combining multiple computational steps into a fast and user-friendly tool. 
- Matsvei Tsishyn, Pauline Hermans, Marianne Rooman, Fabrizio Pucci (2025). Residue conservation and solvent accessibility are (almost) all you need for predicting mutational effects in proteins. Bioinformatics, 41(6), btaf322. https://github.com/3BioCompBio/RSALOR 

```{r}
# Function to load RSALOR benchmarking results
load_rsalor_benchmarking_data <- function(
  file_path, 
  gene, 
  structure_source = NULL, 
  score_col = "RSA.LOR",
  flip_sign = TRUE
) {
  
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_id = mutation_fasta,
      structure_source = structure_source,
      RSALOR = as.numeric(.data[[score_col]])
    )

  if (flip_sign) {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(RSALOR = -RSALOR)
  }

  return(df)
}
```

### 4) GEMME MSA + ProteoCast
- ProteoCast relies on GEMME, a highly efficient, unsupervised, and fully interpretable variant effect predictor (Laine et al., 2019). By focusing on how protein residues segregate along the topology of evolutionary trees, GEMME has proven instrumental for studying protein stability, function, and disease mechanisms in several studies -- see, for instance, Tsuboyama et al., 2023. It was extensively tested against over 2.5M experimental measurements (Abakarova et al., 2023, Laine et al., 2019). It is among the top-performing methods on the widely adopted ProteinGym benchmark. 
- Official GEMMA Link https://www.lcqb.upmc.fr/GEMME/submit.html 
- ProteoCast https://proteocast.ijm.fr/results/search/, give interactive heatmaps + Mutational Landscape + Input Alignment + Raw Score Distribution + Sensitivity profile + 3D Structure
- Load results from ProteoCast, provided both GEMME scores and scores weighted by RSA.

```{r}
# Function to load ProteoCast data
load_proteocast_benchmarking_data <- function(file_path, gene, score_col = "Variant_score", rsa_score_col = "RSA.Variant_score") {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  #df <- read.csv2(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_id = Mutation,
      GEMME = .data[[score_col]],
      ProteoCast = .data[[rsa_score_col]]
    )

  return(df)
}
```

### 5) ProSST-2048 (VenusFactory2)
- It employs a structure quantization module to convert 3D protein structures into discrete tokens using a GVP encoder and k-means clustering, coupled with a Transformer architecture featuring sequence-structure disentangled attention. The model explicitly learns residue-structure relationships, enabling robust predictions even for stability, binding, and expression-related mutations.
- Run ProSST-2048 in VenusFactory2

```{r}
# Function
load_VenusFactory_data <- function(
  file_path,
  predictor = "ProSST_2048",
  structure_source = NULL,
  gene = NULL
) {

  df <- read.csv(
    file_path,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    check.names = FALSE
  )

  m <- stringr::str_match(
    df$Mutant,
    "^([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])$"
  )

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_wt  = m[, 2],
      aa_mut_pos = as.integer(m[, 3]),
      aa_mut_sub = m[, 4],
      aa_mut_id  = paste0(aa_mut_wt, aa_mut_pos, aa_mut_sub),
      structure_source = structure_source
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      !!predictor := `Prediction Score`
    )

  return(df)

}
```

### 7) VESPA
- VESPA is a simple, yet powerful Single Amino Acid Variant (SAV) effect predictor based on embeddings of the Protein Language Model ProtT5. The specifics of VESPA and VESPAl can be found in our paper, Embeddings from protein language models predict conservation and variant effects (Marquet et al., 2021). The performance of VESPA when evaluated against SOTA methods can be seen below.
- https://github.com/Rostlab/VESPA

```{r}
# Function to load VESPA benchmarking scores
load_vespa_full_benchmarking_data <- function(
  file_path,
  gene,
  full_score_col = "VESPA",
  light_score_col = "VESPAl",
  flip_sign = TRUE
) {

  df <- read.csv2(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # ---- Fix Mutant indexing: M0A -> M1A ----
  parsed <- stringr::str_match(df$Mutant, "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Mutant = ifelse(
        !is.na(parsed[,1]),
        paste0(
          parsed[,2],
          as.integer(parsed[,3]) + 1,
          parsed[,4]
        ),
        Mutant
      ),

      # ---- standardized mutation ID ----
      aa_mut_id = Mutant,

      # ---- metadata + scores ----
      gene = gene,
      VESPA = as.numeric(.data[[full_score_col]]),
      VESPAl = as.numeric(.data[[light_score_col]])
    )

  # ---- Optional sign flip ----
  if (flip_sign) {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        VESPA = -VESPA,
        VESPAl = -VESPAl
      )
  }

  return(df)
}
```

### 8) Tranception L
- Tranception, a novel transformer architecture leveraging autoregressive predictions and retrieval of homologous sequences at inference to achieve state-of-the-art fitness prediction performance. 
- https://github.com/OATML-Markslab/Tranception, download the Tranception Large model checkpoint

- Updated Tranception L with and without MSA retrival
  - without MSA retrieval $TranceptionL
  - with MSA retrieval $TranceptionR

  - remove the 1st position M1 to M0

### 9) EVmutation2
- Thomas A. Hopf, Artem Gazizov, Sergio Garcia Busto, Ethan Eschbach, SunJae Lee, Milot Mirdita, Rose Orenbuch, Khaoula Belahsen, David Ross, Chris Sander, Martin Steinegger, Simon d’Oelsnitz, Debora S. Marks. evedesign: accessible biosequence design with a unified framework. bioRxiv 2026.03.17.712115; doi: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.03.17.712115
- https://github.com/debbiemarkslab/EVmutation, This package has been superseded by the EVcouplings package, which covers the full computational pipeline including alignment generation, 3D structure prediction, and more.
- https://evedesign.bio/

```{r}
# Function to load the ESM2 and EVmutation2 prediction results
load_esm2_evMut2_data <- function(file_path, predictor = NULL, gene = NULL) {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(df) <- c("predictor_id", predictor, "predictor_mut_seq")
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      gene = gene,
      # Split predictor_id by "_"
      id_parts = str_split(predictor_id, "_"),
      aa_mut_pos = as.numeric(sapply(id_parts, `[`, 2)),
      aa_mut_wt      = sapply(id_parts, `[`, 3),
      aa_mut_sub     = sapply(id_parts, `[`, 4),
      aa_mut_id  = paste0(aa_mut_wt, aa_mut_pos, aa_mut_sub)
    ) %>%
    select(-id_parts)  # clean up temporary column
  
  return(df)
}
```

### 10) SaProt (650M)
- a “structure-aware vocabulary” that integrates residue tokens with structure tokens. The structure tokens are derived by encoding the 3D structure of proteins using Foldseek. SaProt, a large-scale general-purpose PLM trained on an extensive dataset comprising approximately 40 million protein sequences and structures. 
- Su, J., Li, Z., Tao, T. et al. Democratizing protein language model training, sharing and collaboration. Nat Biotechnol (2025). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-025-02859-7
- https://github.com/westlake-repl/SaProt
- the aa positions need to shift, because the original results always start from 1

```{r}
# Function to load SaProt benchmarking scores
load_saprot_benchmarking_data <- function(file_path, gene, structure_source, score_col = "score") {
  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  #df <- read.csv2(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      gene = gene,
      aa_mut_id= mutation,
      structure_source = structure_source,
      SaProt_650M_AF2 = .data[[score_col]]
    )

  return(df)
}
```

### 11) ESM2 (8M, 35M, 150M, 650M, 3B, 15B)
- SOTA general-purpose protein language model. Can be used to predict structure, function and other protein properties directly from individual sequences. Released with Lin et al. 2022 (Aug 2022 update). our state-of-the-art ESM-2 and ESMFold, as well as MSA Transformer, ESM-1v for predicting variant effects and ESM-IF1 for inverse folding ... 
- 'ESM-2 outperforms all tested single-sequence protein language models across a range of structure prediction tasks. ESMFold harnesses the ESM-2 language model to generate accurate structure predictions end to end directly from the sequence of a protein.'
- https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm?tab=readme-ov-file

```{r}

# Function to prepare DDMut-PPI Affinity predictions
prepare_ddmut_ppi_results <- function(ddmut_df, aa_name_map) {
  ddmut_df <- ddmut_df %>%
    mutate(
      aa_from = aa_name_map[toupper(wild.type)],
      aa_to   = aa_name_map[toupper(mutant)],
      aa_mut_id = paste0(aa_from, res.number, aa_to),
      ddmut_mut_id = paste(chain, aa_mut_id, sep = " ")
    ) %>%
    rename(
      DDMut_PPI = ddmut.ppi.forward.prediction,
      DDMut_PPI_rev = ddmut.ppi.reverse.prediction
    )
  
  return(ddmut_df)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to load and process DDMut-PPI ddG affinity prediction files
load_ddmut_ppi_data <- function(protein_code, base_path = "./data/predictors_data/000_DDMut_PPI_ddG_affinity", aa_name_map) {
  # Construct full path
  path <- file.path(base_path, protein_code)
  
  # List CSV files
  csv_files <- list.files(path = path, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(csv_files) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No files found for", protein_code, "in", path))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Read and combine CSVs
  data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(csv_files, read.csv))
  
  # Process using the provided amino acid mapping
  data <- prepare_ddmut_ppi_results(data, aa_name_map)
  
  # Print duplicate information
  dup_table <- table(duplicated(data$ddmut_mut_id))
  print(paste(protein_code, "- Duplicated ddmut_mut_id:"))
  print(dup_table)
  
  return(data)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to load and process DDMut ddG stability prediction files
load_ddmut_example_data <- function(folder_path) {
  csv_files <- list.files(
    path = folder_path,
    pattern = "\\.csv$",
    full.names = TRUE
  )

  df <- do.call(
    rbind,
    lapply(csv_files, read.csv, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  )

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      ddmut_mut_id = paste0(chain, " ", aa_from, position, aa_to)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::rename(
      DDMut = prediction,
      DDMut_rev = prediction_reverse
    )

  return(df)
}


load_ddmut_data <- function(protein_code, pdb_code, base_path = "./data/predictors_data/000_DDMut_ddG_stability/") {
  # Construct path to folder
  folder_name <- paste0(protein_code, "_", pdb_code)
  path <- file.path(base_path, folder_name)
  
  # List and read all CSV files
  csv_files <- list.files(path = path, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
  if (length(csv_files) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No files found in", path))
    return(NULL)
  }

  data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(csv_files, read.csv))
  
  # Create mutation identifier
  data$ddmut_mut_id <- paste0(data$chain, " ", data$aa_from, data$position, data$aa_to)
  
  # Optionally rename the prediction column
  if ("prediction" %in% colnames(data)) {
    data <- data %>% rename(DDMut = prediction,
                            DDMut_rev = prediction_reverse)
  }
  
  # Report duplicates
  dup_table <- table(duplicated(data$ddmut_mut_id))
  print(paste(folder_name, "- Duplicated IDs:"))
  print(dup_table)
  
  return(data)
}
```

```{r}
# Function to prepare ProteinMPNN_ddG data
prepare_proteinmpnn_ddG_results <- function(df) {
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      mut_id = paste(Pre, Position, Post, sep = ""),
      ddmut_mut_id = paste(Chain, mut_id, sep = " ")
    ) %>%
    rename(
      ProteinMPNN_ddG = ProteinMPNN.ddG.Score
    )
  return(df)
}
```

### 17) ThermoMPNN
- H. Dieckhaus,M. Brocidiacono,N.Z. Randolph, & B. Kuhlman,  Transfer learning to leverage larger datasets for improved prediction of protein stability changes, Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 121 (6) e2314853121, https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2314853121 (2024).

```{r}
# Function to load the ThermoMPNN prediction data and correct the aa positions
load_thermompnn_data <- function(
  file_path, 
  position_offset = 0,
  flip_sign = TRUE
) {

  df <- read.csv(file_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # ---- Standardize column names ----
  names(df) <- c("row", "aa_mut_ID", "ThermoMPNN", "position", "aa_from", "aa_to")

  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      # ---- Fix position ----
      position = as.integer(position) + position_offset,

      # ---- Standard mutation ID ----
      aa_mut_id = paste0(aa_from, position, aa_to),

      # ---- Ensure numeric ----
      ThermoMPNN = as.numeric(ThermoMPNN)
    )

  # ---- Optional sign flip ----
  if (flip_sign) {
    df <- df %>%
      dplyr::mutate(ThermoMPNN = -ThermoMPNN)
  }

  return(df)
}
```

### 00) RSASA, structural baselines
RSASA as baseline, to predicting the mutational effects by surface accessibility;

- RSASA vs Mutations (only single ORF 1aa mutations)
```{r}
# Function to prepare RSASA predictions
prepare_mut_RSASA_baselines <- function(data) {
  
  safe_pmax <- function(df, pattern) {
    cols <- select(df, ends_with(pattern))
    if (ncol(cols) == 0) {
      return(NA_real_)  # no matching columns
    } else {
      return(do.call(pmax, c(cols, na.rm = TRUE)))
    }
  }
  
  data %>%
    filter(aa_mut_class == "Missense") %>%
    mutate(
      #RSASA_monomer_rescaled = safe_pmax(., "_aa_monomer_RSASA2"),
      RSASA_complex          = safe_pmax(., "_binderS_aa_RSASA"),
      #dRSASA_complex         = safe_pmax(., "_binderS_aa_dRSASA"),
      RSASA_monomer          = safe_pmax(., "_aa_monomer_RSASA")
    ) %>%
    select(
      aa_mut_pos,
      aa_mut_gene,
      aa_mut_structure,
      aa_mut_wt,
      aa_mut_sub,
      phix_aa_mut_orf_class,
      fitness_aa_mut,
      
      #RSASA_monomer_rescaled,
      RSASA_monomer,
      RSASA_complex
      #dRSASA_complex,
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Function to process RSASA data
process_RSASA_data <- function(gp_data) {
  # Step 1: Set column names
  names(gp_data) <- c("aa_wt_info", "RSASA", "col_to_remove")
  
  # Step 2: Extract mutation position and mutation wild-type information
  gp_data <- gp_data %>%
    mutate(
      aa_mut_pos = as.numeric(str_split_fixed(aa_wt_info, "`", 2)[, 2]),
      aa_mut_wt = as.character(str_split_fixed(aa_wt_info, "/", 6)[, 5]),
      RSASA = as.numeric(str_sub(RSASA, 1, -2))
    )
  
  # Step 3: Select relevant columns
  gp_data_to_bind <- gp_data %>%
    select(aa_mut_pos, RSASA)
  
  return(gp_data_to_bind)
}
```

### 2) phix174 individual proteins
- most Structure-based predictions, predictions by using PDB or AF3 structures;
- separately merge to protein-structure data.frames, merge fitness and predictions data in proteins data.frame

```{r}
# Function to skip models not applied and to prevent NA and characters in score columns
prepare_structure_predictions_long <- function(df,
                             model_cols,
                             gene_col = "aa_mut_gene",
                             fit_col = "fitness_aa_mut",
                             rescaled_col = "fitness_modelling_rescaled",
                             name_col = "model_name",
                             value_col = "prediction_score") {

  # keep only model columns that exist
  model_cols_present <- intersect(model_cols, colnames(df))

  df %>%
    # Step 1: keep fitness as-is (no rescaling)
    dplyr::mutate(
      !!rescaled_col := .data[[fit_col]]
    ) %>%
    # Step 2: coerce model columns to numeric
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::all_of(model_cols_present),
        ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.))
      )
    ) %>%
    # Step 3: Pivot to long format
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = dplyr::all_of(model_cols_present),
      names_to = name_col,
      values_to = value_col
    )
}
```

```{r}
# Function to process mutant id
add_mutation_columns <- function(df, mutant_col = "mutant") {

  m <- stringr::str_match(df[[mutant_col]], "([A-Z])(\\d+)([A-Z])")

  df$aa_mut_wt  <- m[, 2]
  df$aa_mut_pos <- as.integer(m[, 3])
  df$aa_mut_sub <- m[, 4]
  df$aa_mut_id  <- paste0(df$aa_mut_wt, df$aa_mut_pos, df$aa_mut_sub)

  df
}

technical_control_blat_sign_check_results <- technical_control_blat_sign_check_map %>%
  mutate(
    spearman_r = purrr::map2_dbl(my_col, pg_col, function(col1, col2) {

      x <- technical_control_blat_proteinGym_merged[[col1]]
      y <- technical_control_blat_proteinGym_merged[[col2]]

      keep <- !(is.na(x) | is.na(y))

      if (sum(keep) < 10) return(NA_real_)

      suppressWarnings(cor(x[keep], y[keep], method = "spearman"))
    })
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sign_status = case_when(
      is.na(spearman_r) ~ "NA",
      spearman_r > 0.2 ~ "correct",
      spearman_r < -0.2 ~ "reversed",
      TRUE ~ "unclear"
    )
  )
```

#### 2) Viral proteins records
- reference control, download Zero-shot predictions from proteinGym, pick viral predictions specifically

```{r}
# Function to load proteinGym datasets 
load_proteingym_dataset <- function(file_path, predictors = predictors_tested) {
  
  cols_needed <- c("mutant", "DMS_score", predictors)
  
  df <- fread(file_path, select = cols_needed, showProgress = FALSE)
  
  df <- as.data.frame(df)
  
  df_long <- df %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(predictors),
      names_to = "predictor_col",
      values_to = "prediction"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      dataset = basename(file_path)
    )
  
  return(df_long)
}

# define predictors
predictors_tested <- c("ESCOTT", "PoET", "RSALOR", "GEMME", "ProSST-2048", "ESM-IF1", "MIFST", "VESPA", "VESPAl", "Tranception_L_no_retrieval", "Tranception_L", "SaProt_650M_AF2", "ESM2_8M", "ESM2_35M", "ESM2_150M", "ESM2_650M", "ESM2_3B", "ESM2_15B", "ESM1v_single", "ESM1v_ensemble", "ESM3", "ESMC-300M", "ESMC-600M", "Progen2_large", "Progen2_xlarge")

# load viral predictions
folder_path_proteingym_zero_shot_virus <- "./data/predictors_data/999_ProteinGym_benchmarking/ProteinGym_zero_shot_substitutions_scores_virus"

proteingym_zero_shot_virus <- purrr::map_dfr(files_proteingym_zero_shot_virus, load_proteingym_dataset, predictors = predictors_tested)
```

```{r}
    phix_aa_mut_orf_class = first(phix_aa_mut_orf_class),
```

```{r}
predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind <- predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat %>%
  dplyr::filter(metric == "Spearman_r") %>%

    gene_name,
    predictor_target,

    median_rho = value,
    sd_spearman_rho = NA_real_,

    predictor_input_modality,
    predictor_rank_by_virus,
    predictor_rank_average,
    
    predictor_input_modality_simplified = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("RSA", predictor_input_modality, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "RSA",
      TRUE ~ predictor_input_modality_simplified
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(mean_rho))
```

```{r}
rsa_median_line

# Plot dataframe: one dot per protein per predictor
phix_dot_plot_df <- phix_perf_clean %>%
  #filter(predictor_name != rsa_name) %>%
  group_by(predictor_name) %>%

# summarize the performance for each predictor

  )


# n labels, one per predictor

  distinct(predictor_name, n_proteins) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = max(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.04,

  )


# Vertical dot plot with n labels above each predictor
# 1) plotting overall performance
dot_plot_VEP_evaluation <- ggplot(
  phix_dot_plot_df,
  aes(
    x = predictor_name,
    y = median_rho
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = rsa_median_line,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = median,
    geom = "crossbar",
    width = 0.45,
    color = "red",
    linewidth = 0.35,
    linetype = "solid"
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = phix_dot_plot_df %>% filter(!is_rsa_monomer, !is_rsa_complex),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.75,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = phix_dot_plot_df %>% filter(is_rsa_monomer),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = "red"
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    data = phix_dot_plot_df %>% filter(is_rsa_complex),
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    size = 1.4,
    alpha = 0.85,
    color = "orange"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = phix_n_label_df,
    aes(
      x = predictor_name,
      y = y_pos,
      label = n_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3,
    angle = 90,
    hjust = 0
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = seq(
      floor(min(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) * 10) / 10,
      ceiling((max(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.12) * 10) / 10,
      by = 0.2
    ),
    labels = function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(
      min(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(phix_dot_plot_df$median_rho, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.12
    ),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 15, r = 10, b = 10, l = 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Spearman rho",
    title = "ΦX174 predictor performance by protein",
    #title = expression(Phi*X174~predictor~performance~by~protein),
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Each dot is one protein; dashed line = median RSA (monomer), rho = ",
      round(rsa_median_line, 3)
    )
  )
```

### 2) Pairwise performance comparison
compare ML models VS RSA
```{r}
# check data
head(as.data.frame(predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind), 0)
table(predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind$predictor_name)

# compare to RSA baseline
#rsa_name <- c("RSA (monomer)", "RSA (complex)")
rsa_name <- "RSA (monomer)"


# 1) comparisons by proteins, ML models vs. RSA 
predictions_performance_phix_vs_rsa <- predictions_performance_combined_phix_blat_to_bind %>%
  filter(gene_name != "TEM-1 (Control)") %>%
  select(gene_name, predictor_name, median_rho) %>%
  filter(!is.na(median_rho)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = predictor_name,
    values_from = median_rho
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(gene_name, all_of(rsa_name)),
    names_to = "predictor_name",
    values_to = "method_rho"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(method_rho), !is.na(.data[[rsa_name]])) %>%
  mutate(
    rsa_rho = .data[[rsa_name]],
    delta_vs_rsa = method_rho - rsa_rho,
    outcome_vs_rsa = case_when(
      delta_vs_rsa > 0 ~ "Better than RSA",
      delta_vs_rsa < 0 ~ "Worse than RSA",
      TRUE ~ "Equal to RSA"
    )
  )


# 2) paired RSA-scaled comparison
rsa_baseline <- phix_perf_clean %>%
  filter(predictor_name == rsa_name) %>%
  select(
    gene_name,
    rsa_mean_rho = mean_rho,
    rsa_median_rho = median_rho
  )

phix_vs_rsa <- phix_perf_clean %>%
  filter(predictor_name != rsa_name) %>%
  left_join(rsa_baseline, by = "gene_name") %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(mean_rho),
    !is.na(median_rho),
    !is.na(rsa_mean_rho),
    !is.na(rsa_median_rho)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_mean_vs_rsa = mean_rho - rsa_mean_rho,
    delta_median_vs_rsa = median_rho - rsa_median_rho,

    outcome_mean_vs_rsa = case_when(
      delta_mean_vs_rsa > 0 ~ "Better than RSA",
      delta_mean_vs_rsa < 0 ~ "Worse than RSA",
      TRUE ~ "Equal to RSA"
    ),

    outcome_median_vs_rsa = case_when(
      delta_median_vs_rsa > 0 ~ "Better than RSA",
      delta_median_vs_rsa < 0 ~ "Worse than RSA",
      TRUE ~ "Equal to RSA"
    )
  ) 


# 3) paired RSA-scaled summary
phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired <- phix_vs_rsa %>%
  group_by(
    predictor_name,
    predictor_input_modality,
    predictor_input_modality_simplified
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rho_method = mean(mean_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rho_method = median(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_rho_rsa_matched = mean(rsa_mean_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rho_rsa_matched = median(rsa_median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_delta_mean_vs_rsa = mean(delta_mean_vs_rsa, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_delta_mean_vs_rsa = median(delta_mean_vs_rsa, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_delta_median_vs_rsa = mean(delta_median_vs_rsa, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_delta_median_vs_rsa = median(delta_median_vs_rsa, na.rm = TRUE),

    n_genes_compared = n_distinct(gene_name),

    n_better_than_rsa_median = sum(delta_median_vs_rsa > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_worse_than_rsa_median = sum(delta_median_vs_rsa < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_equal_to_rsa_median = sum(delta_median_vs_rsa == 0, na.rm = TRUE),

    fraction_better_than_rsa_median = n_better_than_rsa_median / n_genes_compared,
    fraction_worse_than_rsa_median = n_worse_than_rsa_median / n_genes_compared,
    fraction_equal_to_rsa_median = n_equal_to_rsa_median / n_genes_compared,

    genes_compared = paste(sort(unique(gene_name)), collapse = ", "),
    genes_better_than_rsa_median = paste(sort(unique(gene_name[delta_median_vs_rsa > 0])), collapse = ", "),
    genes_worse_than_rsa_median = paste(sort(unique(gene_name[delta_median_vs_rsa < 0])), collapse = ", "),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_delta_median_vs_rsa))

phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired


# 4) a paired sign test 
# This is optional, but useful. It asks whether a predictor beats RSA on more genes than expected by chance.
phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired <- phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    sign_test_p_median_vs_rsa = ifelse(
      n_better_than_rsa_median + n_worse_than_rsa_median > 0,
      binom.test(
        x = n_better_than_rsa_median,
        n = n_better_than_rsa_median + n_worse_than_rsa_median,
        p = 0.5,
        alternative = "greater"
      )$p.value,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    sign_test_FDR_median_vs_rsa = p.adjust(sign_test_p_median_vs_rsa, method = "BH")
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_delta_median_vs_rsa))



# 7) strict same-gene comparison across all predictors
common_genes_all_predictors <- phix_perf_clean %>%
  group_by(gene_name) %>%
  summarise(
    n_predictors = n_distinct(predictor_name),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(n_predictors == n_distinct(phix_perf_clean$predictor_name)) %>%
  pull(gene_name)

common_genes_all_predictors


phix_summary_common_genes <- phix_perf_clean %>%
  filter(gene_name %in% common_genes_all_predictors) %>%
  group_by(predictor_name) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rho_phix_common = mean(mean_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_rho_phix_common = median(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),

    sd_mean_rho_phix_common = sd(mean_rho, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_median_rho_phix_common = sd(median_rho, na.rm = TRUE),

    n_genes_common = n_distinct(gene_name),
    gene_names_common = paste(sort(unique(gene_name)), collapse = ", "),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(predictor_metadata, by = "predictor_name") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_rho_phix_common))

phix_summary_common_genes







## Plottings
# 1) barplot of mean_delta_median_vs_rsa
phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired_plot <- phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired %>%
  mutate(
    direction = case_when(
      mean_delta_median_vs_rsa > 0 ~ "Better than RSA",
      mean_delta_median_vs_rsa < 0 ~ "Worse than RSA",
      TRUE ~ "Equal to RSA"
    ),
    predictor_name = fct_reorder(predictor_name, mean_delta_median_vs_rsa)
  )

ggplot(
  phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired_plot,
  aes(
    x = predictor_name,
    y = mean_delta_median_vs_rsa,
    fill = direction
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.5, color = "black") +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0("n=", n_genes_compared),
      hjust = ifelse(mean_delta_median_vs_rsa > 0, -0.15, 1.15)
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Predictor",
    y = expression(Mean~Delta~median~rho~" vs RSA"),
    fill = NULL,
    title = "RSA-scaled predictor performance across ΦX174 proteins",
    subtitle = "Positive values indicate higher performance than RSA on matched proteins"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )



# 2) pairwise comparisons by genes
phix_vs_rsa_bidirectional <- phix_summary_vs_rsa_paired %>%
  select(
    predictor_name,
    predictor_input_modality_simplified,
    n_genes_compared,
    n_better_than_rsa_median,
    n_worse_than_rsa_median,
    fraction_better_than_rsa_median,
    fraction_worse_than_rsa_median,
    mean_delta_median_vs_rsa
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      n_better_than_rsa_median,
      n_worse_than_rsa_median
    ),
    names_to = "comparison",
    values_to = "n_genes"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    direction = case_when(
      comparison == "n_better_than_rsa_median" ~ "Better than RSA",
      comparison == "n_worse_than_rsa_median" ~ "Worse than RSA"
    ),

    fraction = case_when(
      direction == "Better than RSA" ~ fraction_better_than_rsa_median,
      direction == "Worse than RSA" ~ fraction_worse_than_rsa_median
    ),

    n_genes_signed = case_when(
      direction == "Better than RSA" ~ n_genes,
      direction == "Worse than RSA" ~ -n_genes
    ),

    label = paste0(
      n_genes, "/", n_genes_compared,
      " (", round(fraction * 100), "%)"
    )
  )

# heatmap
delta_limit <- max(abs(phix_vs_rsa$delta_median_vs_rsa), na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(
  phix_vs_rsa,
  aes(
    x = gene_name,
    y = fct_reorder(predictor_name, delta_median_vs_rsa, .fun = mean),
    fill = delta_median_vs_rsa
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(delta_median_vs_rsa, 2)),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#4575B4",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#D73027",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-delta_limit, delta_limit),
    name = expression(Delta~median~rho~" vs RSA")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "ΦX174 protein",
    y = "Predictor",
    title = "Gene-wise predictor performance relative to RSA",
    subtitle = "Positive values indicate higher median rho than RSA; negative values indicate lower median rho"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )


# horizontal barplots showing model performance
ggplot(
  phix_vs_rsa_bidirectional,
  aes(
    x = fct_reorder(predictor_name, mean_delta_median_vs_rsa),
    y = n_genes_signed,
    fill = direction
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = label,
      hjust = ifelse(n_genes_signed > 0, -0.05, 1.05)
    ),
    size = 3
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) abs(x),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "Number of ΦX174 proteins",
    fill = NULL,
    title = "Models performance compared to RSA across ΦX174 proteins",
    subtitle = "Positive bars indicate proteins where the predictor outperforms RSA; negative bars indicate proteins where RSA performs better"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```
